punchline: Richard Koch did well at Oxford by deliberately not reading most of his reading list.
thirty_sec: In The 80/20 Principle, Richard Koch recalls noticing at Oxford that exams tested a limited range of topics. Studying past papers, he focused deeply on the key areas and skipped much of the reading list, doing well while working less than many peers. Later he saw the same pattern in consulting and investing. His lesson: find where results really come from, and go deep there.
question: What is your version of the past exam paper, the signal of what's really rewarded?
